settings.scope: credible Linux loader prototype with original unrestricted test mods

M3-W0.evidence: docs/architecture/m3-hook-targets.md and the pinned 26.1.2 hook inventory

M3-W2.evidence: command, event, resource, and data conformance suites

M3-W4.evidence: The conformance suite proves the saved-data model and the process matrix proves the reviewed vanilla save hooks are reachable. Ravel has not yet moved its own versioned bytes through a world save and reload.

M3-W7.evidence: evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json proves the reviewed hook inventory is reachable in a native launch, along with the production screens and stores. It does not prove every required M3 surface natively while M3-W4's Ravel-owned world write remains open.

M3-W8.evidence: The independent prototype review returned FAIL with four findings. Two remain open: M3-W4 lacks a Ravel-owned versioned world write, and M3-W7 did not exercise every required surface natively. Two are resolved: the manifest inventory omission of M3-W0, and the package-schema contradiction, which change rkrpplvwpklskyuwvksvmuuyklkwsqlt closed by migrating schemas/package.schema.json in place so that targets is refused and source declares a repository plus integrity-protected portable files. Clean results: hook integrity passed, safety/layering/ADR conformance passed, and redaction passed. M3-W8 stays open until the two implementation gates close and a later independent review passes.

deviations.summary: The first M3 manifest draft omitted M3-W0 from workPackages even though its gate status appeared elsewhere in the same document. The M3-W8 review treated that as blocking; this revision resolves it by adding M3-W0 to the canonical inventory.

The M3-W8 review found schemas/package.schema.json still required compiled per-target artifacts and could not express the source-only distribution contract ADG-2 selected. Change rkrpplvwpklskyuwvksvmuuyklkwsqlt resolved it as a breaking schema-v1-in-place migration: targets is no longer admitted, source declares a repository and at least one portable file with its SHA-256 digest, and the unsupported-target failure kind was removed with it. The finding is closed and is recorded here so the audit trail keeps it rather than losing it.
M3-W8 found no hook-integrity defect: the reviewed hook inventory, generated lock, transformed-class counts, and callable-target counts reconcile.
M3-W8 found no safety, layering, or ADR-conformance defect in the reviewed prototype stack.
M3-W8 found no redaction defect in the tracked evidence; raw launcher, account, world, and capture material remains outside the repository.

risks.summary: M3-W4 is open. The saved-data model and vanilla hook reachability are proven, but Ravel has not moved its own versioned bytes through an official world save, clean exit, and reload. evidence/m3/profiling-overhead.json also records saved-data footprint as unsupported because that world-write half does not exist.

M3-W7 is open. evidence/m3/linux-process-matrix.json proves all reviewed hook targets are reachable natively and supports the eventual process gate, but it cannot prove every required M3 surface passes natively while M3-W4 remains open.

One excluded diagnostic launch and the first W7 launch remained alive after the normal game shutdown sequence. The accepted W7 relaunch exited naturally, so the recurring post-shutdown futex hang is tracked separately and does not invalidate the matrix's supporting evidence.

attestations.statement: Injected input opened the world through the ordinary title screen, Singleplayer world selection, and Play Selected World path. No quick-play or configuration-injected auto-join route was used.
